settings.heading: How long does an order take?
settings.text: Everything is cut ahead and in stock. Orders leave São Paulo in five working days; hemming adds four.

settings.heading: Can I change or cancel an order?
settings.text: Any time before it ships, in full. Once a garment has been hemmed to your measurement it is yours.

settings.heading: What happens when a season ends?
settings.text: The cloth runs out and the pattern is retired. A garment that earns it stays in the permanent range; the rest do not return.

settings.heading: Do you make anything to measure?
settings.text: Trousers and coats, a few times a year. Write with your measurements and we will say plainly whether it is worth doing.

settings.heading: Ordering
settings.intro: Everything here is answered by a person if you would rather ask.

settings.heading: Where does the cloth come from?
settings.text: Named on the label and on every product page: the mill, the town and the weight. Merino from Biella, linen from Cork, cotton grown in Ceará and woven in São Paulo.

settings.heading: What is the difference between the three cloths?
settings.text: Merino is coating weight and holds its shape. Irish linen creases hard, and is meant to. Organic cotton twill is the mid-weight that takes daily wear.

settings.heading: Can I see the cloth before I buy?
settings.text: Ask and we post a swatch, free, anywhere. It is cheaper for both of us than a return.

settings.heading: Is anything treated or blended?
settings.text: No. Every cloth is a single undyed or piece-dyed natural fibre, and the composition on the label is the whole composition.

settings.heading: How should I wash it?
settings.text: Written on every product page for that cloth. Most of it is a cold machine wash and a line dry; only the coats want dry cleaning, and only once a season.

settings.heading: My linen creased on the first wear. Is that a fault?
settings.text: No, it is what wet-spun linen does. Press it if you like, but the crease is the cloth telling the truth about itself.

settings.heading: Do you repair garments?
settings.text: Free for five years — seams, buttons, linings and moth holes. Post it back, or bring it to the counter at the back of the cutting room.

settings.heading: How is an order sent?
settings.text: Insured and signed for, everywhere. Tracking arrives the morning it leaves São Paulo.

settings.heading: Do you ship outside Brazil?
settings.text: Yes. Duties and import taxes are the customer’s, and we declare the full value — we will not under-declare a parcel.

settings.heading: What is the returns window?
settings.text: Thirty days, unworn, with the tags on, and we pay the return. Garments hemmed to your measurement are final sale, and we say so before you order.

settings.heading: Still unanswered?
settings.intro: A person reads every message. We reply within two working days.
